newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian OLO futures to test support at 119.40.
newsitem.headline: Belgian OLO futures to test support at 119.40.

text.p: Belgian linear bond futures are to test the support line of their 119.40-119.80 point range of the past 11 trading days on Thursday, after bouncing off that level on Wednesday.
A first target is a support line around 119.10, one dealer said.
Front-month OLO futures closed 28 basis points lower at 119.47. Bund futures were down 38 bps in late Wednesday trade.
European bonds were hit after Bundesbank chief economist Otmar Issing said there was no reason to expect further cuts in key German interest rates.
Issing also said German 1996 economic growth would be better than expected.

The 2006 cash bond closed with a yield of 6.09 percent, up from 6.05 Tuesday. The yield premium over equivalent 10-year German bonds narrowed to nine bps from 11. OLOs usually lags Bunds on the way down, causing the spread to narrow.

Dealers said there had been a lot of selling pressure in the 2002 and 2003 area, which is still seen as dear, following a bout of buying by a large domestic player in recent weeks. The 2002 OLO yield closed five bps higher at 5.14 percent.

The six-year bond yields 15 bps less than its German equivalent. The five-year bond yields eight bps over Bunds, making it the only OLO in the two to nine year range with a positive premium over Bunds.
Dealers said the entire German yield curve had flattened somewhat after Issing's comments, while the Belgian curve showed little movement. "Maybe we will catch up tomorrow," one said.
-- Geert De Clercq, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6813, Fax +32 2 230 7710
